name: Regulatory Dependency Mapping
description: Connects a regulator's handbook structure to the obligations, controls, systems, business services and accountable owners a firm has put in place against it. Answers which parts of the business a regulatory change reaches, where control coverage is incomplete, and which shared systems concentrate compliance risk.

Standard.label: Standard
Standard.description: A named regulatory standard, handbook or sourcebook published by a supervisory authority — the highest level of the regulatory hierarchy, e.g. a prudential sourcebook. Sections hang beneath it.

id.description: Short identifier for the standard as the regulator publishes it, e.g. the sourcebook code. Expected to be the prefix that section identifiers are built from.

title.description: Full published title of the standard.

regulator.description: Short code of the supervisory authority that issues and maintains the standard, as the firm records it in its regulatory inventory (e.g. a national conduct or prudential regulator's abbreviation).

jurisdiction.description: Code of the jurisdiction whose law or rulebook gives the standard force, using the firm's own jurisdiction coding (ISO 3166 alpha-2 country codes or supranational codes such as EU).

Section.label: Section
Section.description: A single addressable unit of regulatory text — a chapter, section or subsection of a standard. Sections form the hierarchy of a handbook and are the level at which regulatory change is tracked and obligations are attributed.

id.description: Section identifier exactly as cited by the regulator, including the standard prefix, e.g. a sourcebook code followed by chapter and section numbers. Expected to be unique across all standards.

title.description: Long heading of the section as published, conventionally including the section identifier.

lastUpdated.description: Date on which the section's current text took effect in the handbook — the in-force date of the latest amendment, not the date the amendment was announced or published. Calendar date only; ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD). This is the property regulatory-change analysis filters on.

Obligation.label: Obligation
Obligation.description: A discrete compliance requirement the firm has extracted from a section of regulatory text and holds itself to. One section may yield several obligations; each obligation traces back to exactly one section.

id.description: Firm-assigned identifier for the obligation in its compliance register. Expected to be stable across handbook revisions.

title.description: One-line statement of what the firm must do, phrased as an action.

category.description: Compliance theme the obligation belongs to, from the firm's own taxonomy. This model's vocabulary is capital-adequacy, reporting, governance, conduct, disclosure, operational-resilience, record-keeping.

reportingFrequency.description: How often the obligation falls due, from the vocabulary ongoing, daily, monthly, quarterly, annual, event-driven. 'ongoing' means a continuous standard rather than a periodic submission.

inherentRiskScore.description: Risk of breaching this obligation assessed before any control is taken into account, on a 1-5 scale where 5 is the highest inherent risk. Inherent, not residual — a well-controlled obligation keeps a high score.

Control.label: Control
Control.description: A procedure, check or automated safeguard the firm operates to satisfy one or more obligations. Controls are the layer at which compliance is actually evidenced and tested.

id.description: Firm-assigned identifier for the control in its control inventory.

name.description: Short descriptive name of the control as it appears in the control inventory.

controlType.description: Point in the risk lifecycle at which the control acts, from the vocabulary preventive (stops the failure), detective (finds it after the fact), corrective (remediates it).

automationLevel.description: Degree of human involvement in operating the control, from the vocabulary manual, semi-automated, automated. A manual control may still be recorded against a system used to evidence it.

lastTestedDate.description: Date the control was last tested for operating effectiveness by a second or third line function. Calendar date only; ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD). Not the date the control last ran.

effectivenessScore.description: Assessed operating effectiveness at the last test, on a 1-5 scale where 5 is most effective. Reflects the assessment at lastTestedDate and does not decay on its own.

BusinessService.label: BusinessService
BusinessService.description: A service the firm delivers to clients or to the market, of the kind an operational-resilience framework identifies and sets an impact tolerance for. The point at which regulatory change becomes a business consequence.

id.description: Firm-assigned identifier for the business service in its service catalogue.

name.description: Business-facing name of the service as the firm's service catalogue records it.

criticality.description: Resilience classification of the service, from the vocabulary important-business-service (formally designated, with a board-approved impact tolerance), material, standard.

impactToleranceHours.description: Maximum tolerable duration of disruption to this service, in whole hours measured from the onset of disruption rather than from its detection. Lower means less tolerant.

System.label: System
System.description: An application, platform or infrastructure component that business services run on and that controls are implemented in. Systems depend on other systems, so a failure here propagates.

id.description: Firm-assigned identifier for the system in its configuration management database or application inventory.

name.description: Name of the system as recorded in the application inventory.

hostingModel.description: Where the system runs and who operates it, from the vocabulary on-premise, private-cloud, public-cloud, vendor-saas. Relevant to third-party and ICT concentration analysis.

tier.description: Criticality tier from the firm's IT service management scheme, on a 1-3 scale where 1 is the most critical. Note this runs opposite to the 1-5 risk and effectiveness scales elsewhere in the model.

BusinessUnit.label: BusinessUnit
BusinessUnit.description: An organisational function that holds accountability for obligations and for business services — the answer to 'who has to act' when a regulation changes.

id.description: Firm-assigned identifier for the business unit or function.

name.description: Name of the business unit or function as the firm's organisational register records it.

smfReference.description: Reference to the senior management function accountable for this unit under the applicable individual-accountability regime, in the regulator's own notation. Several units may share one reference where one senior manager covers them all.

sectionInStandard.description: Places a top-level section directly beneath the standard that publishes it. Only sections at the top of a handbook's hierarchy carry this; deeper sections reach the standard through their parent section instead.

sectionInSection.description: Places a section beneath its immediate parent section in the handbook hierarchy, read child to parent. Chaining these from a top-level section reconstructs the full depth of a handbook.

serviceOnSystem.description: States that the business service cannot be delivered without the system. Direct dependencies only; indirect ones are reached by continuing through the system-to-system chain.

systemOnSystem.description: States that the from system requires the to system to function — the to system is upstream. Expected to be acyclic so that dependency chains terminate.

sectionRelated.description: Records a cross-reference made by the citing (from) section to the cited (to) section, so that a change to the cited text is known to reach the citing text.

subsection.description: The specific rule within the cited (to) section that the citing section refers to, in the regulator's own rule notation. Where a section is cited as a whole this is expected to be the section identifier itself.

obligationFromSection.description: Traces the obligation back to the single section of regulatory text it was extracted from. This is the join that turns a handbook change into a compliance impact.

controlSatisfiesObligation.description: States that the control contributes to meeting the obligation, and by how much. An obligation with no incoming SATISFIES is uncontrolled, which is a meaningful finding rather than missing data.

coveragePercent.description: Assessed share of the obligation's requirements this control addresses, as a whole number from 1 to 100. Coverage contributed by all controls on one obligation is expected to sum to at most 100, so a sum below 100 is a residual gap.

serviceGovernedByObligation.description: States that the business service falls within the scope of the obligation, so a change to the obligation changes how the service must be run.

controlOnSystem.description: Names the system the control is operated in or evidenced from. A control with no such link is operated entirely outside the application estate.

unitAccountableForService.description: Names the business unit answerable for running the business service. Exactly one unit is accountable for each service, whatever the number of units involved in delivering it.

unitAccountableForObligation.description: Names the business unit answerable for meeting the obligation. Distinct from accountability for a service: the unit that owns an obligation is often not the unit that runs the services the obligation governs.
